items.title: J. Leo Rayhill interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 23, 2007
items.q: The Johnny Guarneri is a great example, who ... played with Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw.

ctx.x: I know exactly what you’re saying. Do you play mostly CDs now?

Mostly CDs. But every show has at least between two and four LPs that I work at. Because I feel that there’s so many jazz musicians that are not available on CD that we need to listen to. I hate to think that the music is gone and forgotten. And I try to work those in. And I think they’re very good. The Johnny Guarneri is a great example, who © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
played with Benny Goodman and Artie Shaw. There’s nothing on CD. It’s all on LPs and I try to work him in from time to time. He was a good piano player.
